# Neuro-Symbolic Architecture Overview

`specshiny` separates **user intent**, **interface presentation**, and
**statistical execution** to resolve the flexibility-versus-accessibility
trade-off in statistical Shiny applications without ever evaluating untrusted
language-model output:

```text
[Plain-English Prompt / Refinements]
        |
        v  Pluggable Translator (translator_rule / translator_openai / translator_ollama)
[Typed Specification IR: spec_ir v1.1.0 (YAML / JSON)]
        |
        v  Pure-R Schema & Statistical Sanity Validator (validate_spec_ir)
        +----------------------------------------------+
        |                                              |
        v                                              v
[Dynamic Minimal bslib/Shiny UI]             [Deterministic Compilers]
- spec_to_controls() (active only)           - compile_r_script() (AST-verified)
- mod_spec_composer_* / controls_*           - compile_quarto_report() (sanitized)
- spec_history() Undo / Redo + Diffs         - export_spec_bundle() (SHA-256)
```

## Trust Boundaries & Safety Guarantees

1. **Zero `eval(parse())` of Untrusted Input:** Translators emit declarative
   JSON/YAML only; YAML parsers explicitly enforce `eval.expr = FALSE` and
   block `!expr` tags.
2. **Closed Schema Allowlists:** `validate_spec_ir()` rejects unknown nested
   properties, non-ASCII homoglyphs, leading dots, reserved words, and
   non-positive-definite covariance/correlation matrices via eigenvalue checks.
3. **Mandatory Static AST Gate (`verify_compiled_r_ast()`):** Every compiled R
   script is parsed statically (zero execution) and verified against a closed
   positive allowlist (`base`, `stats`, `lme4`, and script-local helpers).
   Calls to `eval`, `parse`, `system`, `system2`, `do.call`, `source`,
   `unlink`, `file.remove`, `get`, `assign`, `:::`, dynamic callees, and
   higher-order banned references (`lapply(x, system)`) are unconditionally
   rejected.
4. **Quarto, LaTeX, and XSS Defenses:** `compile_quarto_report()` neutralizes
   inline knitr expressions, uses 6-tilde outer YAML fences, strips dangerous
   LaTeX directives (`\write18`, `\input`, `\immediate`), and escapes HTML
   angle brackets.

# Specification Grammar (`spec_ir` v1.1.0) Cheat Sheet

| Section | Core Fields | Guardrails Enforced |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `hierarchy` | `levels` (1 or 2), `n_obs`, `n_clusters`, `cluster_size`, `cluster_size_dist` (`fixed`/`normal`/`poisson`), `cluster_size_sd`, `icc` | `n_obs >= 5`; `n_clusters >= 3`; `cluster_size > q_rand`; `icc` in `[0, 1)`; `cluster_size_sd > 0` |
| `predictors` | `name`, `level`, `distribution` (`normal`/`binary`/`uniform`), `centering`, `role` + optional `predictor_corr` | Pure ASCII identifiers; unique names; `sd > 0`; `0 < prob < 1`; `min < max`; PD `predictor_corr` (same-level only) |
| `outcome` | `name`, `family` (`gaussian`/`binomial`/`poisson`), `link`, `residual_sd`, `error_dist` (`normal`/`t`/`skewed`), `error_df`, `error_skew` | Valid family-link pair; `residual_sd > 0`; `error_df > 2`; `error_skew` in `[-4, 4] \ {0}` |
| `effects` | `intercept`, `fixed`, `interactions` (`spec_interaction()`), `focal_predictor`, `random` (`intercept`, `slopes`, `corr_matrix`) | Level-1 predictors only for random slopes; PD `corr_matrix`; distinct interaction terms |
| `missingness` | `mechanism` (`none`/`MCAR`/`MAR`), `rate`, `target`, `auxiliary`, `strength` | `rate` in `[0, 0.95)`; `rate == 0` when `none`; MAR requires valid `auxiliary` and non-zero `strength` |
| `estimator` | `engine` (`lm`/`glm`/`lmer`/`glmer`), `reml`, `conf_level` | Family/level/random-effects compatibility; `conf_level` in `(0.5, 1)` |
| `simulation` | `n_reps`, `seed`, `alpha`, `parameter_grid` | `n_reps` in `[1, 100000]`; `alpha` in `(0, 0.5)`; grid cardinality `<= 250` |

# Core Workflow Reference

## 1. Translate, Refine, and Manage Undo/Redo History

```{r workflow-demo}
prompt <- paste(
  "2-level power analysis for the cross-level interaction between x1 and z1 of 0.30",
  "with 50 schools, 20 students per school, cluster size sd 5, ICC 0.2,",
  "random slope for x1, t-distributed errors df 5, 200 replications"
)

tr <- nl_to_spec(prompt)
hist <- spec_history(tr$spec)

ref <- refine_spec(tr$spec, "increase clusters to 70 and add 15% MAR missingness")
history_push(hist, ref$spec, label = "70 schools + 15% MAR")
format_diff_summary(ref$diff)
history_summary(hist)
```

## 2. Minimal Dynamic UI Synthesis

```{r ui-demo}
d_simple <- spec_to_controls(new_spec_ir())
d_rich   <- spec_to_controls(ref$spec)
c(single_level_controls = d_simple$control_count,
  multilevel_interaction_controls = d_rich$control_count)
```

## 3. Deterministic Compilation, AST Audit & Study Bundles

```{r bundle-demo}
r_code <- compile_r_script(ref$spec)
ast_res <- verify_compiled_r_ast(r_code)
c(ast_safe = ast_res$safe, expressions = ast_res$n_expressions)

bdir <- file.path(tempdir(), "specshiny_guide_bundle")
export_spec_bundle(ref$spec, bdir, overwrite = TRUE)
ver <- verify_spec_bundle(bdir)
ver$valid
unlink(bdir, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Composing Dynamic `bslib` / Shiny Apps

Connect the three reusable modules through two shared `shiny::reactiveVal`
objects (`spec_rv` and `last_diff_rv`) plus a `spec_history()` stack:

- `mod_spec_composer_ui()` / `mod_spec_composer_server()` --- NL prompt
  compilation, presets, iterative refinements, clarifications, and defaults
  rationale.
- `mod_spec_controls_ui()` / `mod_spec_controls_server()` --- minimal active
  `bslib` widgets, loop-free bidirectional sync, undo/redo buttons, visual
  diff badges, and inline guardrail alerts.
- `mod_spec_preview_ui()` / `mod_spec_preview_server()` --- live mathematical
  equations, YAML/JSON IR, AST-verified R script, budget-capped quick preview
  runner (`max_preview_reps`, `max_preview_n`, `max_preview_seconds`), Quarto
  `.qmd` report, and download handlers.

Launch the bundled flagship demo interactively with `run_specshiny_demo()`.
